name: Tulsi
description: Tulsi, or Holy Basil, is one of the most sacred plants in Hindu tradition and a cornerstone of Ayurvedic medicine. It is an aromatic shrub with green or purple leaves and small flowers. Known as the 'Queen of Herbs,' Tulsi has been revered for over 3,000 years for its remarkable healing properties.
traditional_uses: Respiratory support – relieves cough, cold, bronchitis, and asthma
Adaptogen – helps the body cope with stress
Digestive aid – relieves bloating and indigestion
Antimicrobial – effective against bacteria, fungi, and viruses
Oral health – used in toothpastes and mouthwashes

cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical; thrives in warm, humid conditions
cultivation.soil: Well-drained, fertile loamy soil with pH 6–7.5
cultivation.harvesting: Leaves can be harvested 6–8 weeks after planting

habitat: Native to the Indian subcontinent; widely cultivated in tropical Asia
safety_notes: Generally safe for most adults. Pregnant women should avoid large medicinal doses. May have mild blood-thinning properties. For educational purposes only — consult a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner before use.

name: Neem
description: Neem is a fast-growing tree native to the Indian subcontinent, often called the 'Village Pharmacy' of India. Every part of the tree — leaves, bark, seeds, and oil — has medicinal value. It has been used in Ayurvedic medicine for over 4,500 years. Known for its bitter taste and remarkable antimicrobial properties.
traditional_uses: Skin disorders – treats acne, eczema, psoriasis, and fungal infections
Dental care – used in traditional toothbrushes (datun) and toothpastes
Anti-diabetic properties – helps regulate blood sugar

cultivation.soil: Sandy loam to clay loam; tolerates alkaline and poor soils

habitat: Native to Indian subcontinent and Myanmar; naturalized in tropical Africa and Americas
safety_notes: Neem is toxic in large quantities. Neem oil should never be taken internally. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid medicinal neem. Not recommended for children under 12 in concentrated forms. For educational purposes only.

name: Ashwagandha
description: Ashwagandha is one of the most powerful adaptogenic herbs in Ayurvedic medicine. Its name means 'smell of horse' in Sanskrit, referring to the herb's unique smell and its ability to impart the strength of a horse. The root is the primary medicinal part. It is classified as a Rasayana (rejuvenating tonic) in Ayurveda.
traditional_uses: Adaptogen – manages stress, anxiety, and cortisol levels
Cognitive function – improves memory, focus, and mental clarity
Energy and vitality – combats fatigue and improves stamina
Hormonal balance – supports thyroid and adrenal function
Reproductive health – traditionally used as an aphrodisiac
Sleep quality – promotes restful sleep (somnifera = sleep-inducing)

cultivation.climate: Dry, subtropical climate; tolerates arid conditions
cultivation.soil: Sandy loam, well-drained, low fertility preferred

habitat: Native to India, North Africa, and Mediterranean; grows in dry regions
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy (may cause miscarriage). May interact with thyroid medications, immunosuppressants, and sedatives. Not recommended for people with autoimmune conditions without professional guidance. For educational purposes only.

name: Turmeric
description: Turmeric is a rhizomatous plant widely used as a spice, dye, and medicine. The bright yellow-orange rhizome contains curcumin, the primary bioactive compound responsible for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. It has been used in Ayurveda for thousands of years and is known as the 'Spice of Life.'
traditional_uses: Anti-inflammatory – curcumin is a powerful COX-2 inhibitor
Wound healing – applied topically for cuts and burns
Digestive health – stimulates bile production and digestion
Joint health – used for arthritis and rheumatic conditions

cultivation.soil: Well-drained loamy or clay loam soil rich in organic matter
cultivation.harvesting: 9–10 months after planting; leaves turn yellow-brown

habitat: Native to South and Southeast Asia; widely cultivated in tropical regions
safety_notes: Generally safe in culinary amounts. High doses may cause gastrointestinal issues. May interact with blood thinners. Avoid supplements during pregnancy in large amounts. For educational purposes only.

name: Ginger
description: Ginger is one of the world's most widely used medicinal plants and culinary spices. The underground rhizome contains gingerols and shogaols, bioactive compounds with potent anti-nausea, anti-inflammatory, and digestive properties. In Ayurveda, fresh ginger (Ardraka) and dry ginger (Shunthi) are treated as distinct medicines.
traditional_uses: Nausea and vomiting – motion sickness, morning sickness
Digestive stimulant – improves appetite and digestion
Anti-inflammatory – for arthritis and muscle pain
Respiratory – relieves cold, cough, and sore throat

cultivation.soil: Rich loamy soil, well-drained with high organic content
cultivation.watering: Regular; keep moist but not waterlogged

habitat: Native to Southeast Asia; now cultivated throughout tropical regions worldwide
safety_notes: Safe in culinary amounts. May interact with blood thinners and diabetes medications. Avoid large amounts during pregnancy. May cause heartburn in sensitive individuals. For educational purposes only.

name: Amla
description: Amla is a sacred fruit tree in Ayurveda, considered one of the most powerful Rasayanas. It is the richest natural source of Vitamin C, which remains stable due to tannins even after heat processing. The sour, astringent fruit is used in Triphala (a classical Ayurvedic formulation) and Chyawanprash.
traditional_uses: Vitamin C powerhouse – immune system support
Hair health – prevents hair fall, premature greying; used in Amla oil
Digestive tonic – relieves constipation and hyperacidity

cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical; drought-tolerant once established
cultivation.soil: Loamy to sandy loam; slightly acidic to neutral pH

habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical India, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia
safety_notes: Generally very safe. May cause constipation if consumed in large amounts without adequate water. May lower blood sugar — diabetics on medication should monitor. For educational purposes only.

name: Brahmi
description: Brahmi is a small, creeping perennial herb that grows in wet, marshy conditions. Named after Brahma, the Hindu god of creation, it is revered as a brain tonic in Ayurveda. Active compounds called bacosides improve nerve signal transmission and support brain health. It is one of the most studied Ayurvedic herbs in modern neuroscience.
traditional_uses: Cognitive enhancement – memory, learning, and concentration
Neuroprotective – protects brain cells from oxidative stress
Hair growth when applied topically as Brahmi oil

cultivation.soil: Moist, loamy or muddy soil near water bodies
cultivation.watering: High moisture; can grow in shallow water

habitat: Wetlands, marshes, and water margins across India, Asia, Australia, and Americas
safety_notes: Generally safe. May cause nausea in some individuals when taken on an empty stomach. High doses can cause GI issues. May potentiate sedative drugs. For educational purposes only.

name: Shatavari
description: Shatavari, meaning 'she who possesses a hundred husbands,' is the premier Ayurvedic herb for women's reproductive health. It is a climbing plant with small pine-needle-like leaves and white flowers. The tuberous roots are the medicinal part. It is classified as a Rasayana with adaptogenic and immunomodulatory properties.
traditional_uses: Women's health – hormonal balance, menstrual regulation, menopause support
Lactation support – promotes breast milk production
Reproductive tonic – fertility support for both men and women
Digestive healing – soothes ulcers and hyperacidity

cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical; thrives in warm, humid conditions
cultivation.soil: Loamy, well-drained soil with good organic content
cultivation.watering: Moderate; regular watering during dry periods

habitat: Found throughout India, Sri Lanka, and the Himalayas in low forest areas
safety_notes: Avoid if allergic to asparagus family. May interact with diuretics. Those with kidney disease should use cautiously. Generally safe but consult a practitioner for therapeutic doses. For educational purposes only.

name: Haritaki
description: Haritaki is one of the three fruits in Triphala, the most famous Ayurvedic formulation. Called the 'King of Medicines' in Tibet and the 'Mother of all Medicines' in traditional systems, it is considered the most important herb in Ayurveda. The dried fruit is wrinkled, brown, and rich in tannins and polyphenols.
traditional_uses: Digestive rejuvenator – relieves constipation, regulates bowel movement
Detoxification – cleansing the colon and digestive tract
Oral health – gargling for mouth ulcers and gum disease

cultivation.climate: Tropical dry and moist deciduous forests; semi-arid
cultivation.soil: Various soil types; sandy loam to clay loam
cultivation.propagation: Seeds; grafting for faster fruit production

habitat: Native to India, Nepal, Myanmar, Sri Lanka; grows in tropical forests
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy (strong laxative effect). May cause loose stools in high doses. Take with caution if dehydrated or on laxatives. For educational purposes only.

name: Giloy
description: Giloy is a climbing shrub with heart-shaped leaves and yellow-green flowers. The stem is the primary medicinal part, though leaves and roots are also used. Known as 'Amrita' (divine nectar) in Ayurveda, it is a powerful immunomodulator and adaptogen. It gained global attention during COVID-19 for its immune-boosting properties.
traditional_uses: Immune modulator – one of the strongest immunostimulants in Ayurveda
Fever management – antipyretic properties (used in dengue, malaria recovery)

cultivation.climate: Tropical and subtropical; adaptable to varied conditions
cultivation.soil: Well-drained, loamy soil; can grow in rocky terrain
cultivation.harvesting: Stem harvested throughout the year; best in summer

habitat: Native to tropical India; found throughout India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar
safety_notes: May stimulate the immune system — avoid in autoimmune conditions (lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) without professional guidance. May lower blood sugar — monitor if diabetic. For educational purposes only.

name: Aloe Vera
description: Aloe vera is a succulent plant with thick, fleshy leaves containing a clear gel. The inner gel and yellow latex (found just below the skin) have distinct medicinal properties. Kumari in Ayurveda means 'young girl,' referring to its ability to restore youth and vitality. It is one of the most extensively researched plants in modern herbal medicine.
traditional_uses: Skin healing – burns, sunburns, wounds, and skin irritations
Digestive health – relieves constipation (latex), soothes gut inflammation
Hair conditioning – reduces dandruff, promotes hair growth

cultivation.soil: Sandy, well-draining soil; cactus mix ideal
cultivation.watering: Infrequent; allow soil to dry between waterings
cultivation.propagation: Offsets (pups) from the base of the plant
cultivation.harvesting: Outer leaves from mature plants (3+ years)

habitat: Native to the Arabian Peninsula; now cultivated worldwide in warm climates
safety_notes: The yellow latex can cause severe diarrhea — avoid internal use of latex. Topical gel is generally safe. Avoid oral use during pregnancy. May interact with laxatives and anti-diabetic drugs. For educational purposes only.

name: Moringa
description: Moringa is called the 'Miracle Tree' because virtually every part is edible or medicinal. It is one of the most nutrient-dense plants on Earth, containing 7× more vitamin C than oranges, 4× more calcium than milk, and 3× more potassium than bananas. In Ayurveda, it is classified as a Rasayana and used for over 300 diseases in traditional texts.
traditional_uses: Edema and water retention – diuretic properties

cultivation.soil: Sandy or loamy, well-drained; poor soil tolerance
cultivation.harvesting: Leaves harvested 60 days after planting; pods after 6–8 months

habitat: Native to sub-Himalayan region of India; widely cultivated in tropical Africa and Asia
safety_notes: Roots contain spirochin (potentially toxic nerve-paralyzing agent) — avoid root consumption in large amounts. Generally safe when leaves and pods are consumed as food. Avoid high-dose supplements during pregnancy. For educational purposes only.

name: Fenugreek
description: Fenugreek is an annual herb with distinctive maple-syrup aroma from the compound sotolone. Both leaves and seeds are used as food and medicine. The seeds contain galactomannans, a soluble fiber that slows glucose absorption, making fenugreek one of the best-studied anti-diabetic plants. It is commonly used in Indian cooking and traditional medicine.
traditional_uses: Blood sugar control – anti-diabetic properties via galactomannans
Digestive aid – relieves constipation and gastritis
Lactation support – galactagogue that increases milk production
Skin and hair health when applied topically

cultivation.soil: Well-drained loamy soil; slightly alkaline preferred
cultivation.harvesting: Leaves: 4–6 weeks; Seeds: 4 months after sowing

habitat: Mediterranean region and Western Asia; widely cultivated in India
safety_notes: May cause uterine contractions — avoid therapeutic doses during pregnancy. Can interact with anti-diabetic medications (risk of hypoglycemia). May cause maple syrup odor in sweat and urine. For educational purposes only.

name: Licorice
description: Licorice root is one of the world's oldest herbal remedies. The root contains glycyrrhizin, which is 50 times sweeter than sugar. In Ayurveda, Yashtimadhu (meaning 'sweet wood') is classified as a Rasayana. It is a primary ingredient in many Ayurvedic preparations for respiratory and digestive health.
traditional_uses: Respiratory health – cough, sore throat, bronchitis, asthma
Adrenal support – fatigue and adrenal insufficiency
Oral health – antibacterial for dental plaque
Voice tonic – used by singers in India

cultivation.soil: Deep, well-drained sandy loam; alkaline tolerance

habitat: Native to Southern Europe, Middle East, and Central Asia; cultivated in India
safety_notes: Avoid prolonged high-dose use — can raise blood pressure, cause fluid retention, and lower potassium. Not recommended for people with hypertension, kidney disease, or during pregnancy. For educational purposes only.

name: Peppermint
description: Peppermint is a hybrid mint species known for its refreshing menthol aroma. The essential oil contains high concentrations of menthol, which activates cold receptors and produces the characteristic cooling sensation. It is widely used in Ayurveda for its carminative, analgesic, and antimicrobial properties.
traditional_uses: Digestive relief – IBS, bloating, gas, nausea
Headache relief – topical application of oil on temples
Pain relief – menthol for muscle aches

cultivation.soil: Moist, well-drained loamy soil; rich in organic matter
cultivation.harvesting: Before flowering; cut 1/3 of plant height

habitat: Originated in Europe; naturalized worldwide in moist habitats
safety_notes: Do not apply peppermint oil directly to the face of infants or young children — can cause breathing difficulties. Avoid in acid reflux/GERD. May interact with certain medications. For educational purposes only.

name: Cardamom
description: Cardamom is known as the 'Queen of Spices.' It is a perennial herb with long leaves and small green pods containing aromatic seeds. The essential oil contains 1,8-cineole and terpinyl acetate. It is used extensively in Ayurveda as a digestive, carminative, and rejuvenating herb. It is also a key ingredient in Chyawanprash.
traditional_uses: Digestive stimulant – relieves indigestion, gas, and nausea
Respiratory health – expectorant for cough and congestion
Detoxification – enhances liver and kidney function

cultivation.climate: Cool, shaded tropical forests; high altitude (600–1500m)
cultivation.soil: Rich loamy forest soil with high organic matter
cultivation.harvesting: Pods harvested by hand before fully ripe; 3–4 years to first harvest

habitat: Native to Western Ghats, India; cultivated in Kerala, Guatemala, and Sri Lanka
safety_notes: Generally safe in culinary amounts. High doses may cause gallstone colic in those with existing gallstones. Avoid large therapeutic doses during pregnancy. For educational purposes only.

name: Black Pepper
description: Black pepper is one of the most widely traded spices and has been used since ancient times. Piperine, its active compound, not only gives pepper its pungency but also significantly enhances the bioavailability of other herbs and drugs (notably curcumin from turmeric by 2000%). In Ayurveda, Maricha is classified as an Agni (digestive fire) enhancer.
traditional_uses: Bioavailability enhancer – improves absorption of other medicines
Respiratory – relieves cough, cold, and sinusitis
Analgesic – pain relief topically and internally

cultivation.soil: Laterite clay to well-drained loamy soil; slightly acidic
cultivation.sunlight: Partial shade; grows as a vine on trees

habitat: Native to Malabar Coast, Kerala, India; now cultivated in Vietnam, Indonesia
safety_notes: May cause burning sensation in gastric conditions. Avoid high doses if you have peptic ulcers. Piperine can alter the pharmacokinetics of medications significantly — inform your doctor. For educational purposes only.

name: Cumin
description: Cumin is a slender annual herb with thread-like leaves and small white or pink flowers. The seeds (technically fruits) are the medicinal and culinary part. Cuminaldehyde and other volatile oils give it its distinctive aroma. In Ayurveda, Jiraka is a classic digestive and carminative herb used in formulations like Jeerakadyarishta.
traditional_uses: Digestive health – relieves bloating, gas, and indigestion
Lactation support – increases breast milk production
Iron supplement – rich in iron for anemia

cultivation.climate: Semi-arid, hot dry climate; cool winters
cultivation.soil: Sandy loam, well-drained; drought tolerant

habitat: Native to Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean; major production in India (Rajasthan, Gujarat)
safety_notes: Generally very safe. May slow blood clotting — avoid large amounts before surgery. Possible allergy in those sensitive to the Apiaceae family. For educational purposes only.

name: Coriander
description: Coriander is an aromatic annual herb where both leaves (cilantro) and seeds are used medicinally and culinarily. The leaves have a fresh, citrusy aroma while seeds have a warm, spicy flavor. In Ayurveda, Dhanyaka (seeds) are particularly valued as a digestive, cooling, and detoxifying herb.
traditional_uses: Digestive cooling herb – relieves burning sensation in gut
Heavy metal chelation – helps remove heavy metals from body

cultivation.climate: Cool season; 17–27°C optimal; dislikes extreme heat
cultivation.soil: Sandy loam to loam; well-drained; moderately fertile
cultivation.watering: Moderate; avoid water stress during flowering

habitat: Native to southwestern Asia and Mediterranean; widely cultivated globally
safety_notes: Some people have a genetic variant causing coriander leaves to taste soapy. Possible allergy in Apiaceae-sensitive individuals. Generally very safe in culinary amounts. For educational purposes only.

name: Hibiscus
description: Hibiscus is a large, ornamental shrub with striking red flowers. The flowers, leaves, and roots all have distinct medicinal applications. The deep red calyx of Hibiscus sabdariffa (Roselle) is widely used to make herbal teas with potent antioxidant properties. In Ayurveda, Japakusuma is used primarily for hair, skin, and heart health.
traditional_uses: Hair health – prevents hair fall, conditions hair, reduces dandruff
Blood pressure management – clinical evidence for antihypertensive effect
Skin care – brightens skin, reduces inflammation

cultivation.soil: Well-drained, loamy, slightly acidic to neutral soil
cultivation.harvesting: Flowers harvested when fully open; year-round in tropics

habitat: Native to tropical Asia; widely cultivated as ornamental and medicinal plant worldwide
safety_notes: May lower blood pressure — monitor if on antihypertensive medications. Avoid during pregnancy (emmenagogue and possible uterotonic effects). May interfere with hormonal medications. For educational purposes only.
